Day 1
From Hotel: 24 min · 7 min → Peristyle of Diocletian's Palace
1. Peristyle of Diocletian's Palace
The outdoor ceremonial courtyard at the heart of a Roman imperial palace built around 305 AD — café tables and street musicians now occupy the space where emperors once processed, with Egyptian sphinxes still standing watch.

2 min · 1 min → Cathedral of Saint Domnius
2. Cathedral of Saint Domnius
One of the world's best-preserved Roman mausoleums, built as Diocletian's tomb in the 4th century and converted into a cathedral by the 7th — the octagonal bell tower climbs to panoramic views over Split and the Adriatic.

3. Temple of Jupiter
A near-intact 4th-century Roman temple tucked inside the palace warren — the barrel-vaulted ceiling, ornate friezes, and a headless Egyptian sphinx guard what was later converted into a baptistery; one of the finest small Roman interiors in existence.

1. Meštrović Gallery
Croatia's greatest sculptor designed this white-stone villa as his own home and studio — 200 bronze and marble works displayed across terraces and salons overlooking the Adriatic; one of Europe's most personal art museums.

Split's forested peninsula park rising 178 m above the city — pine-shaded paths lead to medieval hermit chapels and a summit belvedere with sweeping views over the Dalmatian islands, with walking trails starting right beside the Meštrović Gallery.

2. Narodni Trg
Split's medieval public square — flanked by a 15th-century town hall and a Gothic clock tower; locals call it Pjaca and it has been the city's social heart since the Middle Ages, hosting markets and public debates for six centuries.

Day 4
From Hotel: 33 min → Cathedral of Saint Lawrence
1. Cathedral of Saint Lawrence
The masterpiece of Romanesque-Gothic Dalmatia — begun in 1213 on the site of a Saracen-sacked Early Christian cathedral, its west portal carved by Master Radovan in 1240 is the finest sculpture of its era in Croatia; the 47-meter bell tower offers panoramic views over the UNESCO island and the Adriatic.

2. Kamerlengo Castle
A 15th-century Venetian defensive fortress anchoring the southwest corner of the Trogir island — the circular tower and curtain walls that once held off Ottoman fleets now host open-air summer concerts; panoramic views from the ramparts span the islands and the Adriatic coast.

A UNESCO World Heritage island the size of a city block — Romanesque palaces, Venetian loggias, Gothic churches, and medieval fortifications compressed into a pedestrian labyrinth with 2300 years of continuous habitation; the John Paul II waterfront square and the city walls are the best vantage points.

Day 5
From Hotel: 14 min → Salona
1. Salona
The ancient Roman capital of Dalmatia, birthplace of Emperor Diocletian — an archaeological park of 64 hectares in modern Solin with a forum, theatre, Early Christian basilicas, city walls, and a 15,000-seat amphitheatre; at its peak the city held 60,000 inhabitants.
Read more
Salona archaeological park entry · 4.5 · armus.hr

~2 hr
Supilova ul. · Solin
17 min → Split Archaeological Museum
2. Split Archaeological Museum
Croatia's oldest museum, founded in 1820 — 150,000 artifacts spanning prehistoric settlements through Greek colonization, Roman provincial life, and Early Christian Dalmatia; the lapidary garden holds the largest outdoor collection of Roman stonework in Croatia, with inscriptions and sarcophagi from Salona.

15 min · 9 min → Vestibule
3. Vestibule
A roofless 4th-century domed antechamber between the Peristyle and Diocletian's private apartments — a 17-meter circular hall with an open oculus and four niched alcoves for imperial statues; the extraordinary acoustics attract local klapa singers whose harmonies fill the stone dome.

Day 6
From Hotel: 36 min → Omiš
1. Omiš
Croatia's medieval pirate town at the Cetina mouth — local corsairs dominated Adriatic shipping for two centuries from this gorge-entrance harbor; the clifftop Mirabela Fortress 200 meters above offers sweeping views over the canyon, river mouth, and Dalmatian islands.
Read more
Mirabela Fortress entry · 4.6 · omis.hr
Daily 8:30am - 10:00pm
~2 hr
Vangrad 1 · Omiš
17 min · 2 min → Cetina River Canyon
2. Cetina River Canyon
Dalmatia's most dramatic river gorge — the Cetina cuts through 200-meter limestone cliffs west of Omiš, narrowing above emerald water that draws kayakers, rafters, and zip-liners; the canyon mouth where the river meets the sea is one of the most striking geological sights on the Adriatic coast.
Read more

Local Tastes
Peka
Lamb or veal slow-cooked for hours under a cast-iron bell buried in embers with potatoes, herbs, and vegetables — the definitive Dalmatian feast dish; must be ordered 24 hours ahead at most restaurants.
Konoba Fetivi · Konoba Varoš
Pasticada
Split's signature Sunday dish — beef marinated for days then braised in a sweet-sour sauce of prunes, wine, and vinegar, served over handmade gnocchi; intensely flavored and labor-intensive.
Šperun Restaurant · Konoba Fetivi
Gregada
Ancient Dalmatian fish stew from Hvar — white fish simmered gently with potatoes, olive oil, garlic, and white wine; a dish of elegant restraint where ingredient quality does all the work.
Villa Spiza · Šperun Restaurant
Picigin
Not food but an essential taste of Split culture — a uniquely Croatian ball-juggling game played standing in the Bačvice shallows, dating from 1908 and recognized as UNESCO intangible heritage. Watch locals before joining in.
Bačvice Beach
Dingač
Croatia's most prestigious red wine — Plavac Mali grapes from the sun-baked cliff vineyards of the Pelješac peninsula; full-bodied, structured, and best paired with grilled meats or aged sheep cheese.
Bokeria Kitchen & Wine · Šperun Restaurant
Fritule
Small fried dough balls flavored with lemon zest, brandy, and raisins — Split's traditional street sweet, found year-round at bakeries and especially beloved at the Christmas Advent market on the Riva.
Pazar Green Market · Riva Promenade
Food Delivery
Wolt
Foreign number: not required. — sign-up runs on Google, Apple, Facebook or email with no phone field at all, so no verification code is sent.
Helsinki-founded delivery platform with the widest restaurant selection in Split; covers local Dalmatian konobas, pizzerias and fast-food spots across the Manuš, Grad and Spinut neighbourhoods. Reliable for same-neighbourhood delivery within 30–40 minutes.
wolt.com
Glovo
Foreign number: not required. — it signs in with Google, Facebook or email, and a phone sign-up takes any prefix with the code by SMS or WhatsApp.
Spanish-founded platform covering restaurants, grocery stores and convenience items across Split and the wider coastal area; broader category mix than Wolt on some routes. Useful for picking up Croatian pantry staples or snacks on a longer self-catering stay.
glovoapp.com

Getting Around
Bolt
Foreign number: accepted.
Split's most-used ride-hailing app with reliable coverage across the city; upfront fares quoted before booking with no surge pricing on standard routes. A practical option for longer hops between Meštrović Gallery, Marjan Hill and the ferry terminal.
bolt.eu
Uber
Foreign number: accepted.
Widely available ride-hailing option in Split with confirmed fares before booking; comparable pricing to Bolt on most central routes. Worth comparing both apps for trips between the Old Town and outlying neighbourhoods during peak summer season.
uber.com

Day Trips by Train
Solin · 10 min
Roman Salona — the ancient capital of Dalmatia, with a 60,000-seat amphitheatre, city walls, basilicas and the mausoleum of Emperor Diocletian, all just outside town.
book at: Omio
Kaštela · 20 min
Seven medieval castle-villages strung along a coastal bay — each Kaštel built by a different noble family in the 15th and 16th centuries, with intact towers and walls running directly to the water's edge. Alight at Kaštel Stari.
book at: Omio
Šibenik · 1h 30 min
Historic Dalmatian town with a UNESCO-listed cathedral and the gateway to Krka National Park — a comfortable half-day rail excursion with return.
book at: Omio
Knin · 1h 45 min
A medieval fortress town perched on a sheer rock above the Krka canyon — the largest fortress in Croatia, and the junction where the Zagreb and Šibenik rail lines meet in the Dalmatian hinterland.
book at: Omio
Zagreb · 6h 30 min
The scenic daytime rail journey to Croatia's capital winds through the Lika mountains — best paired with a hotel night in Zagreb rather than used as a day trip.
book at: Omio

Worth Knowing

On Split

Diocletian built his retirement palace and never expected anyone to actually live in it. Within 200 years, refugees fleeing the collapse of nearby Salona moved inside the walls and started cooking dinner between the columns. They never left.

The people of Split have been improvising inside a Roman emperor's house for 1700 years — which is why the city feels less like a museum and more like a palimpsest, each century's handwriting still visible on the same walls. Nowhere else in the world do you sit at a café table that is also, technically, a 4th-century imperial audience hall.
